run.question: We got a customer complaint about slow response times in Europe. The customer mentioned seeing request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 in their error page. Find what happened with this request and which service had the issue.

report.summary: The request ID the customer quoted exists in exactly one indexed log document: an ERROR from service "auth" in region "eu-west" at 2026-11-18T14:49:47Z on endpoint /api/v2/auth/validate, response_time_ms=15847, user_id customer-39284, whose message reads "Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts." So the service that had the issue on this request is auth (EU / eu-west), and the failure was an ~15.8 s authentication timeout in its LDAP-dependent validation path, ending in a failed customer login. Of 1,621 log documents in the authorized window, this is the only ERROR and the only document with a request_id; eu-west is the only region whose response_time_ms deviates from 150 ms (max 15847, avg 207.9) while the other five regions are flat at 150 ms, so the evidence shows one anomalous request, not a broad measured regional latency shift. Counter-checks: the cluster's fault-injection flags in otel-demo/flagd-config are all defaultVariant "off" and none targets auth or LDAP; all 32 pods are Running with 0 restarts; no Kubernetes workload, Service, namespace or Endpoint named auth or ldap exists in this cluster, so the failing auth service and its LDAP backend are outside this cluster's inventory. Jaeger and Prometheus were unreachable throughout (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace, span-metric, RPC or error-rate corroboration and no latency baseline could be obtained.

claims.text: The only document carrying request_id REQ-EU-8K4M2 is in index app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 at @timestamp 2026-11-18T14:49:47Z, level ERROR, service "auth", region "eu-west", endpoint "/api/v2/auth/validate", response_time_ms 15847, user_id customer-39284, message "Authentication request timeout - request ID REQ-EU-8K4M2 took 15847ms to respond. LDAP backend connection pool exhausted. Customer authentication failed after retry attempts."
Across all 1,621 log documents in the authorized window the cardinality of request_id is 1, i.e. REQ-EU-8K4M2 is the only request identifier present in this log corpus.
Level breakdown of the 1,621 documents is 1,620 INFO and exactly 1 ERROR; the single ERROR document is the REQ-EU-8K4M2 auth timeout.

Per-region response_time_ms statistics (2026-11-14T17:26Z–2026-11-23T17:26Z): eu-west has 271 docs with min 150, max 15847 and avg 207.92 ms, while ap-northeast, ap-south, eu-central, us-east and us-west each have 270 docs with min = max = 150 ms. The 15,847 ms request is the only sample above 150 ms in the dataset.

In the four hours around the incident (2026-11-18T12:00Z–16:00Z) the only eu-west log document returned is the REQ-EU-8K4M2 auth ERROR itself; no other eu-west service logged a request in that window.

The queried cluster contains no workload named auth or ldap: the 24 Deployments (including kube-system and local-path-storage) and 29 Services in the queried namespaces include only the otel-demo services (ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, load-generator, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping, flagd, jaeger, otel-collector, kube-state-metrics, prometheus, prometheus-readonly-proxy, valkey-cart, alertmanager) plus coredns/metrics-server/local-path-provisioner; existing namespaces are default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo.
All 32 pods in the cluster (otel-demo workloads plus kube-system/local-path-storage) are in phase Running with container restartCount 0 at query time; no pod shows a crash or restart.

Every fault-injection flag in the otel-demo/flagd-config ConfigMap (productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage, imageSlowLoad) has state ENABLED with defaultVariant "off"; no flag refers to auth, LDAP or authentication.

The Prometheus alerting rules held in the otel-demo/prometheus ConfigMap cover only CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh (service_name="checkout", span CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, error ratio > 0.5) plus OpsPilot self-monitoring rules; there is no rule for auth, authentication or LDAP latency/errors.

The 15,847 ms response and failed login for REQ-EU-8K4M2 originated in the auth service's LDAP-dependent validation path: its connection pool to the LDAP backend was exhausted, so the request timed out and the customer's retries also failed. This rests on the auth service's own ERROR message; no LDAP-tier or auth-tier telemetry was available to confirm the pool state independently.

Rejected: that an otel-demo feature-flag fault injection caused the auth slowdown. All flags in otel-demo/flagd-config are set to defaultVariant "off", and none of them names auth, authentication or LDAP.
Rejected: that a pod crash or restart in the cluster produced the failure. All 32 pods are Running with restartCount 0, and no pod in otel-demo carries a name matching auth or ldap.

Counter-evidence against reading this as a broad European latency degradation: 1,620 of the 1,621 documents are INFO "Request completed successfully" records all reporting exactly 150 ms, eu-central is likewise flat at 150 ms, and eu-west's elevated average (207.92 ms) is produced entirely by the single 15,847 ms auth document. The log corpus therefore shows one anomalous request, not a measured multi-request trend.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable for every attempt in this Run (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace/span graph exists for REQ-EU-8K4M2; it cannot be confirmed whether the identifier corresponds to a trace, nor which downstream spans were slow.

Prometheus was unreachable for every attempt (execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so traces_span_metrics_calls_total, rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count / rpc_server_duration_milliseconds_bucket and http_server_request_duration_seconds_count for auth could not be read; no error-rate reading and no comparable latency baseline were obtainable.

No LDAP backend is observable: there is no ldap workload, Service, Endpoint, pod, ConfigMap or log stream in the cluster, so the "LDAP backend connection pool exhausted" statement is only the auth service's own log assertion and the pool state itself was not verified.

Container logs retained by the cluster start around 2026-11-23 (fetch_pod_logs on frontend and frontend-proxy returned only lines after the requested 2026-11-18T14:00–15:30Z window), so no application log from any cluster pod covers the incident second.
The Kubernetes events query over all namespaces returned zero events inside the authorized window, so no event-based corroboration of a change, restart or fault at 2026-11-18T14:49:47Z exists.
The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment/config change can be checked immediately before 2026-11-18T14:49:47Z.

The 1,620 non-error documents are spread across 1,620 per-region/per-service/per-day indices (app-185-geo-*), each holding one document; the corpus is sparse and cannot establish per-minute request volume, so the number of other EU requests affected by the same condition is unknown.
All Kubernetes object state was read at 2026-11-23 (after the incident) and cannot prove the cluster's state on 2026-11-18T14:49:47Z.
next_steps: Pull auth-service and LDAP-side metrics/logs from the eu-west stack that produced app-185-geo-eu-west-auth-2024.01.05 for 2026-11-18T14:49:47Z: LDAP connection-pool saturation, pool wait time, and other /api/v2/auth/validate requests in the same minute.
Restore Prometheus reachability and compare auth latency and error rate around 2026-11-18T14:49Z against a same-length baseline period before the request.
Restore Jaeger reachability and search spans for service auth (or the frontend request carrying REQ-EU-8K4M2) to see the LDAP call duration and whether sibling requests were also affected.
Confirm with the platform owner whether region "eu-west" maps to a separate deployment of auth outside the examined cluster, since no auth or ldap workload exists in this cluster's inventory.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: The tool filtered @timestamp to the query window; this filter cannot be turned off.

content:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
